translations.answer: No. The author continued to explicitly state the issue after correcting the unit understanding, and the maintainer only responded that they are investigating the Isaac Lab implementation, and then closed the issue without providing the reason, patch, or validation. Therefore, this behavior must continue to be marked as unresolved, and one cannot infer that it has been fixed by simply closing the issue.
translations.applicability: Only explains the unresolved behavior in the specified Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab environment; other versions must be minimally reproducible.
translations.credibility.rationale: The answer has not closed the loop or there is a conflict; the current situation is only forming a problem clue; no reproducible reproduction record has been formed yet.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author clipped the DCMotor output to non-negative values and reset the friction/damping; the remaining over-limit issues were handed over to the maintainer.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The author first verified the unit and magnitude of max_angular_velocity, rather than just checking the velocity_limit/velocity_limit_sim of the DCMotor.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: The unit mismatch caused a return to normal behavior, and the force over-limit behavior was recorded separately.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The unit issue was addressed by explaining max_angular_velocity in degrees per second, and the target physical upper limit was converted and configured afterward.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab commit 09590912792d4421c84f053c5c13c31391bb5c30; Isaac Sim 4.5.0-rc.36; Windows 11 Pro 23H2; RTX 4060 Laptop; CUDA Toolkit 11.8.
translations.details.limits.0: The original post did not provide a specific value for max_angular_velocity or a retest curve after correction.
translations.details.limits.1: One cannot equate the issue closure with the force over-limit being resolved.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author admitted the error was due to their configuration; the maintainer did not respond to the remaining over-limit issue, and the issue was closed later.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does the flywheel appear to decelerate during the decay of the applied torque?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why does the angular velocity exceed max_angular_velocity when applying torque, but comply with it after the torque is removed?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Misinterpreting the simulation limit as rad/s could result in an executioner constraint difference of about 57.3 times the real-world limit; units should be standardized and independent limit testing should be performed before deployment.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The author confirmed max_angular_velocity=100 in degrees, and tested it at a low value for the flywheel.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The internal cause of the over-limit during force application was not determined in the original thread.
translations.details.symptoms.0: All explicit friction and damping are set to 0; the DCMotor torque is clipped to non-negative values, but the flywheel speed decreases during the torque decay phase.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The angular velocity exceeds max_angular_velocity when applying torque, but decreases to the configured value during coasting.
translations.media_summaries.0: The original post's curve was explained by the author in the text: the torque decreases after about 100 ms, and the speed is in line with it; the torque becomes zero around 170 ms, and the speed stabilizes afterward; the values in this card were not added from pixel-level image readings, and the unit conclusion was based on the author's subsequent text verification.

translations.source.title: Isaac Sim's max_angular_velocity unit and common angular units are inconsistent, and the torque over-limit is still unexplained.
translations.title: Is this thread explaining why the angular velocity exceeds max_angular_velocity during torque application and only complies after the torque is removed?
